HANDOFF for DrWrinch

Source: HANDOFF.md

Last touched: 2026-05-19 in a session run from ~/repos/fully_specified_bf/. Pick up from here in a fresh Claude session run from ~/repos/DrWrinch/.

What DrWrinch is

The R package implementing Lopez, Bowers, and Gajardo Cooper (2026), “Fully specified Bayes factors for process tracing.” Named after Dorothy Maud Wrinch (1894–1976; joint papers with Harold Jeffreys in the early 1920s developed the framework that later became Jeffreys’s theory of Bayes factors).

Companion package DrBristol (at ~/repos/DrBristol) implements p-value methods for the same class of problems. DrBristol is mature, GitHub-only, named after Muriel Bristol; DrWrinch is its Bayes-factor sibling. Do not merge the two.

The paper lives at ~/repos/fully_specified_bf. Treat the paper as the source of truth for notation and methodology; DrWrinch is the companion code. Integration of DrWrinch into the paper is appendix-only — see the project memory at ~/.claude/projects/-Users-jwbowers-repos-fully-specified-bf/memory/project_drwrinch_paper_integration.md. An appendix section now exists in ~/repos/fully_specified_bf/Paper/appendix.qmd showing how to reproduce the running example with DrWrinch.

Open user decisions awaiting answers (Shiny app)

A planning agent produced a full implementation plan for the Shiny app in PLAN_SHINY.md. The architectural shape is settled (inst/shiny/ with run_app() launcher, deploy via rsconnect, Suggests-only deps). Six decisions are open:

A. Plot library. ggplot2 (recommended; already in Suggests, smaller deploy) or plotly (interactivity).

B. Model layout. Side-by-side cards (recommended; matches “compute both” vignette guidance) or tabs.

C. Advanced inputs. Hide theta_cut, prior_a, prior_b behind an Advanced accordion (recommended) or always-visible.

D. Urn-undefined messaging. Settled: mandatory friendly prose when y_R > y_W + 1; the binomial card still renders.

E. shinyapps.io account. The user needs to confirm whether a personal account exists or to sign up.

F. CRAN submission timing. Plan recommends submitting 0.0.0.9002 to CRAN first (clean four-function package), then adding run_app() in 0.0.1 afterward.

When resuming: ask the user which way A, B, C, E, F go. Then begin Phase 1 of PLAN_SHINY.md.

How to resume

  1. Read in order: this file; PLAN_SHINY.md; ~/repos/ai_workflow/CLAUDE_CODING.md (the user’s code-work rules — tests-before-implementation, pause for review at checkpoints, devtools::document() and devtools::check() before complete, “why” comments at branch points).
  2. Read R/*.R and tests/testthat/*.R to understand what’s already in the package.
  3. Ask the user to answer Decisions A, B, C, E, F. (D is settled.)
  4. Phase 1 of PLAN_SHINY.md: write tests/testthat/test-app_helpers.R first. Pause for review before implementing.

Constraints inherited from the paper repo’s CLAUDE.md and memory

  • No unicode. ASCII only in any file you write or edit. --- for em dash, -- for en dash, -> for arrow, " and ' straight quotes, ... for ellipsis. (Exception in the paper’s evalues.qmd and appendix.qmd: Spanish names with accented characters are OK there. Does not apply to DrWrinch files.)
  • No methodological tribalism. Use Bayes factors as a tool, not a philosophical commitment. Do not introduce “Bayesian” labels.
  • No athletic/defense metaphors for thresholds. BFs do not “clear” or “withstand” thresholds; they are “above” or “below” them.
  • Plain language at branch points. Avoid “is appropriate,” “is reasonable,” structural metaphors (“load-bearing,” “scaffolding”). Name what depends on what.
  • R package work follows CLAUDE_CODING.md. This rule is durable — the user enforced it mid-session; tests must come before implementation, check() before complete, “why” comments at branch points.

DrWrinch and the paper repo

The paper repo’s renv currently has DrWrinch installed locally (via renv::install("local::~/repos/DrWrinch")) so the new appendix section renders. The renv lockfile was not snapshotted, so other machines rebuilding the paper would need to install DrWrinch first. The user has not pushed DrWrinch to GitHub yet — the install_github("bowers-illinois-edu/DrWrinch") line in the appendix will fail until that repo exists.

When the user is ready, the GitHub creation and push can happen from either session; flag it before doing it (it’s a public action).
